context:
Context: Enumerations are bounded to application-owned production/test source of the tracked Apollo modules unless dependencies or generated mechanisms are explicitly requested. Packaged framework evidence supplements those questions. No ambient env/secret values are assumed.
Profile: apollo-portal runs with spring.profiles.active=github,auth (github also activates the mysql profile group); apollo-adminservice and apollo-configservice run with github.
Read-only except AQ-049, whose patch must be applied only in a disposable checkout. No permission to start external services or read process secrets.

prompts: Which modules make up Apollo, where is its build entry point, and which dependencies bring in Spring Boot and Spring Cloud?

Which beans are declared in the production package com.ctrip.framework.apollo.portal.component, directly in that package only, without subpackages? Separate component classes, @Bean methods and beans produced by a FactoryBean, and give their names and scope.

Why does com.ctrip.framework.apollo.portal.component.UnifiedPermissionValidator end up in the Spring context of apollo-portal: which annotations, stereotypes or component scanning rules make that happen?

Show the grounds for registering or skipping it and the limits of that conclusion.

What is injected into the userInfoHolder parameter of the constructor of com.ctrip.framework.apollo.openapi.v1.controller.ReleaseController under github,auth? Show the candidates and why this particular bean is chosen.
